headline: Riyadh's King Khalid Airport partially reopens amid Houthi missile threats
summary: The airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday after a deadly attack earlier this month, though Houthi rebels continue to warn that the site remains a military target.
details: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has partially resumed operations at two terminals following a suspension caused by a deadly attack earlier this month.
Terminal 1 is now designated for domestic flights, while Terminal 2 handles international flights operated by national carriers.
The reopening comes despite renewed warnings from Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree, who stated the airport remains a 'military target' and is not safe.
The airport had previously halted operations on October 10 after a Houthi attack that killed 13 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest incident in the kingdom in over a decade.
Saudi Arabia has intercepted multiple waves of missiles and drones, including 10 ballistic missiles fired toward southern Saudi Arabia and others targeting Riyadh.
Recent clashes have seen shrapnel from intercepted missiles injure two people and damage residential buildings and vehicles in Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah.
The conflict has escalated after Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast, threatening the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical global shipping route.
The renewed fighting has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022, as Saudi Arabia continues its intervention in the Yemeni civil war.
caption:

headline_marked: 3 men get [[life imprisonment for gang-raping]] woman on moving bus
headline: 3 men get life imprisonment for gang-raping woman on moving bus
summary: A Tangail court sentenced a bus driver, conductor, and an associate to life in prison and fined them Tk 2 lakh each for the assault and robbery of a passenger.
details: A Tangail Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal has sentenced three men to life imprisonment for the gang rape of a female passenger on a moving bus.
The convicts include the bus driver, Md Altaf (25), the conductor, Sagar alias Sajib Matubbar (24), and another bus helper, Md Rabbi (21).
The incident occurred on January 14 this year when the victim boarded a Savar Paribahan bus from Mirpur to Ashulia.
The suspects allegedly raped the woman inside the vehicle at the Chandra Bus Stand in Gazipur and robbed her of gold earrings, an iPhone 13 Pro, and cash.
The victim managed to escape near the Karatia underpass in Tangail the following day and alerted highway police, leading to the arrest of the accused.
The court delivered the verdict today following the testimony of 15 witnesses, and the convicts have been sent to Tangail District Jail.
caption:
Three men have been sentenced to life in prison for gang-raping a passenger on a moving bus and robbing her of her valuables.

A Tangail Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal has sentenced three men to life imprisonment for the gang rape of a female passenger on a moving bus.

The convicts include the bus driver, Md Altaf (25), the conductor, Sagar alias Sajib Matubbar (24), and another bus helper, Md Rabbi (21).

The incident occurred on January 14 this year when the victim boarded a Savar Paribahan bus from Mirpur to Ashulia.

The suspects allegedly raped the woman inside the vehicle at the Chandra Bus Stand in Gazipur and robbed her of gold earrings, an iPhone 13 Pro, and cash.

The victim managed to escape near the Karatia underpass in Tangail the following day and alerted highway police, leading to the arrest of the accused.

The court delivered the verdict today following the testimony of 15 witnesses, and the convicts have been sent to Tangail District Jail.
